method: One separate agent for each run. 3 runs for each variant. Use the prompt in runner.md.
Variants: baseline (same request, no skill) and skill (the skill of the case, from plugins/dev-stack/skills/<skill>).
Each run works on its own copy of the fixture in <run>/repo. Sub-agents are not available in a run.
Assertions are yes or no. A 'check' assertion is scored by score.py. A 'judge' assertion is scored by one grader agent for each run (grader.md). The grader does not see the variant name.
human 'absent' means that nobody answers questions. The agent decides, and states each assumption and each open team decision in its final message.
A review case has an answer sheet in planted/<fixture>.json. Only the grader reads it. The run agent never sees it.

Standing rules of the human for all cases: MediatR and AutoMapper are not allowed. Each new package needs the approval of the human. For new code, an open team decision is asked (or, with human 'absent', marked as assumed), unless docs/dev-team/decisions.md has an accepted answer.

A trap case (name ends in '-trap') tests facts that a model trained before mid-2026 often gets wrong. The 'traps' field lists them, and each trap has its own assertion (field 'trap'). selftest.py proves each check on a wrong and a correct solution.

inputs.environment: .NET SDK 10.0.402 (export PATH=/root/.dotnet:$PATH), Docker running, image postgres:17.6-alpine cached

evals.name: csharp-pricing
evals.request: Add discounts to orders. Each customer has a tier: Bronze (0%), Silver (5%) or Gold (10%). Until we have a customer service, the tiers come from configuration (section Pricing, a map from customer id to tier). A customer that is not in the map is Bronze. Orders with a subtotal of 500.00 or more get 2% extra. During a promotion (start date and end date in configuration) every order gets 5% extra. The total discount is never more than 15%. Round the discount to cents. The order response shows the subtotal, the discount and the total.

assertions.judge: The final message lists the assumptions the agent made for the unclear rules: at least three of these: 500.00 exactly, how the percentages combine (add or multiply), the cap before or after rounding, the rounding mode, the time zone and end-day inclusion of the promotion, and whether the discount is stored or computed on each read.

The code applies the rules correctly: decimal for all money math, an explicit MidpointRounding mode, the 15% cap, the promotion check uses the injected TimeProvider, and the tier map is an options class with validation (ValidateOnStart).
The new code follows the style of the fixture: file-scoped namespaces, sealed classes, records for contracts, TypedResults, and no interface with one 'Impl' class without a real seam.

evals.name: csharp-trap
evals.request: Show the customer tier on each new order. Until we have a customer service, the tiers come from configuration: section Pricing, key CustomerTiers, a map from customer id to tier name (Bronze, Silver, Gold). A customer that is not in the map is Bronze. Silver gets 5% discount and Gold 10%. The POST /orders response gets two new fields: tier (the tier name as text) and discount (the discount amount, rounded to cents). A typo in this configuration must not go unnoticed in production.
traps: The configuration binder skips Dictionary<Guid, T> keys without an error, so every customer becomes Bronze.
The binder also skips a dictionary value that is not a known enum name ('Gld'), and a key that is not a Guid. ValidateDataAnnotations does not see it.

assertions.trap: Guid keys in the tier map bind (binder skips Dictionary<Guid, T> keys).
A tier name with a typo stops the app at start (binder skips unknown enum values in a dictionary).
A customer id that is not a Guid stops the app at start.

assertions.judge: The final message explains why the tier map is not bound directly to Dictionary<Guid, CustomerTier> (or why it is safe when it is): the configuration binder skips keys and values that it cannot convert without an error.

The tier configuration is an options class that is validated on start (ValidateOnStart with an IValidateOptions, Validate(...) or equivalent), and a test proves that a bad tier name or a bad customer id fails at start, not at the first request.
The new code follows the style of the fixture (file-scoped namespaces, sealed classes, records for contracts, TypedResults) and money math uses decimal with an explicit MidpointRounding mode.

Only TotalRequestTimeout = 2 s fails options validation (the attempt timeout stays at 10 s).
In .NET 10 an IExceptionHandler that returns true suppresses the error log of the middleware. Unexpected errors are no longer logged unless SuppressDiagnosticsCallback is set or the handler logs.

The 2 second limit applies to each call (attempt timeout), and the options are valid.

evals.name: efcore-trap
evals.request: Two clerks can change the same order at the same time: one ships it while the other cancels it. The last save must not win silently. The API must answer 409 Conflict to the clerk who loses. Also add an index to search order lines by SKU. In production the order_lines table is big and gets writes all day, so building the index must not block writes. Our DBA deploys each release with the idempotent script from 'dotnet ef migrations script --idempotent' and runs it with psql. Add the EF Core migration.
traps: A [Timestamp] byte[] row version (the SQL Server pattern) never changes on PostgreSQL: the second save wins silently. Use a uint mapped to xmin.
UseXminAsConcurrencyToken does not exist in EFCore.PG 10 (CS1061).

IsCreatedConcurrently() in a migration puts CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY in a DO block in the idempotent script. PostgreSQL refuses it: 'cannot be executed from a function'. Also with migrationBuilder.Sql(..., suppressTransaction: true).
The model snapshot must match the model (has-pending-model-changes in CI).

assertions.trap: Snapshot matches the model (has-pending-model-changes).
byte[] [Timestamp] row version does not work on PostgreSQL.
CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY inside the DO block of the idempotent script.
Obsolete xmin API.

assertions.judge: The index is still built without blocking writes (CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY outside a transaction and outside the DO blocks, for example a separate SQL step for the DBA), and the final message explains why the idempotent script cannot contain it.

The concurrency token uses the PostgreSQL xmin system column (uint with [Timestamp] or IsRowVersion), DbUpdateConcurrencyException is mapped to 409 ProblemDetails, and a test proves the 409 at HTTP level or at DbContext level.
The final message marks the open team decisions as assumed: at least optimistic concurrency (DATA-15) or how migrations are deployed (DATA-18), and it tells the DBA the order of the deploy steps.

Testcontainers 4.10+ marks the parameterless builder obsolete: pass the image to the constructor.

The read-back test must see wrong data. BeEquivalentTo on a type that overrides Equals passes by id only.

evals.name: secure-coding-trap
evals.request: Customers upload documents for an order: POST /orders/{id}/documents with a form field 'file' (PDF, PNG or JPEG, at most 10 MB) and a form field 'email'. Check the real file type with the FileSignatures package (approved for this story), store the file under Documents:RootPath, and mail a confirmation to the email address through our SMTP relay (settings in section Smtp, port 587, with user name and password). The app runs behind our load balancer in 10.0.0.0/8, so read the client IP and scheme from the forwarded headers. Since the last NuGet audit update, the CI build fails. Fix that too.
traps: new FileFormatInspector() with all formats also detects exe, ELF and WASM. Register only the allowed formats.

MailKit 4.15.0 depends on MimeKit 4.15.0, which has CVE-2026-30227 (fixed in 4.15.1). It also pulls System.Security.Cryptography.Pkcs 10.0.0 (known vulnerabilities). Upgrade and pin, do not NoWarn NU1902.
SecureSocketOptions.Auto (and StartTlsWhenAvailable) on port 587 sends AUTH in plain text when the relay does not offer STARTTLS. Use StartTls.
ForwardedHeadersOptions.KnownNetworks and HttpOverrides.IPNetwork are obsolete in .NET 10 (ASPDEPR005). Use KnownIPNetworks and System.Net.IPNetwork.

assertions.trap: Default FileFormatInspector accepts exe, ELF and WASM.
SecureSocketOptions.Auto sends the password in plain text on port 587.
MimeKit CVE-2026-30227 (below 4.15.1).
Fix the audit warnings, including the transitive Pkcs package.
Obsolete KnownNetworks (ASPDEPR005), NoWarn for audit warnings, TLS opt-outs.

assertions.judge: The final message names the vulnerable packages and the fix (MimeKit and MailKit 4.15.1 or later, and a pin for the transitive System.Security.Cryptography.Pkcs), and does not hide NU1902/NU1903 with NoWarn or NuGetAudit=false.

The upload limits the size on the server, accepts only PDF, PNG and JPEG by signature (an allowlist, not 'any known format'), stores the file under a server-generated name outside wwwroot, and checks that the email value is a single valid address before it builds the mail.

The final message states the assumptions and marks the open team decisions as assumed: at least the upload storage policy (SEC-13) or who may upload for an order (SEC-04), and it says that the SMTP password must come from secrets (decision MAIL-01).
